title: Set CloudWatch log group retention
description: Updates RetentionInDays on a CloudWatch log group via an asynchronous Cloud Control update.

params.name: region
params.description: Region the log group is in

params.name: retention_days
params.description: Retention period in days; CloudWatch Logs accepts only its documented discrete values

outputs.name: ErrorCode
outputs.description: Failure code when the operation fails, empty otherwise

outputs.name: Identifier
outputs.description: Log group name the request targets

outputs.name: OperationStatus
outputs.description: IN_PROGRESS, SUCCESS, FAILED, PENDING or CANCEL states

outputs.name: RequestToken
outputs.description: Token to poll the request with

template:
UPDATE awscc.logs.log_groups
SET PatchDocument = string('[{"op":"replace","path":"/RetentionInDays","value":{{retention_days}}}]')
WHERE region = '{{region}}'
AND Identifier = '{{log_group_name}}'
RETURNING
  ErrorCode,
  EventTime,
  Identifier,
  Operation,
  OperationStatus,
  RequestToken,
  ResourceModel,
  RetryAfter,
  StatusMessage,
  TypeName;
notes: The response is a progress event, not the updated resource: OperationStatus is typically IN_PROGRESS with a RequestToken. Poll the token with aws/cloud_control/resource-request-by-token (or scan recent requests with aws/cloud_control/resource-requests-by-status) until OperationStatus is SUCCESS or FAILED. The PatchDocument is an RFC 6902 JSON Patch array against the resource's current state, wrapped in string(...); the same pattern updates any mutable property of any AWS resource exposed through Cloud Control. RetentionInDays accepts only the discrete values CloudWatch Logs supports (1, 3, 5, 7, 14, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, 365, 400, 545, 731, 1096, 1827, 2192, 2557, 2922, 3288, 3653); other values fail the update.
